title: Surat al-Nur: When Children Reach Puberty
source: The Qur'an, Surat al-Nur

quotation.english: And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission [to enter] as those before them asked permission.

why_it_matters: The Qur'an makes reaching puberty the point at which a child leaves the legal status of childhood and is addressed as an adult. Childhood therefore ends at puberty, not at a later fixed age such as fifteen.

title: Sunan Abi Dawud: The Command to Pray at Seven
source: Abu Dawud al-Sijistani (d. 275 AH), Sunan Abi Dawud — Prophetic Sunnah

quotation.english: Command your children to pray when they are seven years old, discipline them for it when they are ten, and separate them in their beds.

why_it_matters: The Prophet made seven the first age at which a child is addressed with a religious command, which presupposes discernment. A discerning child needs teaching and upbringing, a role the jurists assign to the father.

title: Fatwa of the Grand Mufti of Egypt Muhammad Bakhit (1917): The Boy Goes to His Father at Seven and the Girl at Nine
source: Egyptian Dar al-Ifta — Grand Mufti Muhammad Bakhit al-Muti'i, 1917; official collection of the Fatwas of Dar al-Ifta (Egypt)

quotation.english: 2 – The mother has no right of custody over the children after they leave the age of custody. … It is stated in Article 391 of the Personal Status [rules] that the custody period of a boy ends when he reaches seven years, and the custody period of a girl ends when she reaches nine years; the father may then take them from the custodian, and if he does not ask for them he is compelled to take them. If the child has neither father nor grandfather, he is handed to the nearest agnatic relative or to the guardian if a boy, and the girl is not handed to anyone other than a mahram.

why_it_matters: An official Egyptian fatwa states the original Egyptian rule: women's custody ends at seven for the boy and nine for the girl, after which the father takes the child and is even compelled to do so.
evidence_level: Official fatwa of the State Mufti

title: World Health Organization: Childhood Ends at Ten
source: World Health Organization (WHO), Adolescent health — United Nations specialized agency, Geneva

quotation.original: Adolescence is the phase of life between childhood and adulthood, from ages 10 to 19.

why_it_matters: The WHO places the start of adolescence at ten, so a fifteen-year-old is in the middle of adolescence, not in childhood.
evidence_level: Official definition of a UN agency

title: UNICEF: The United Nations Defines Adolescents as Those Aged 10 to 19
source: UNICEF — Division of Data, Analytics, Planning and Monitoring, 2024 — United Nations

quotation.original: Defined by the United Nations as those between the ages of 10 and 19, adolescents experience a transition period between childhood and adulthood and with it, significant growth and development.

why_it_matters: The United Nations' own statistical definition treats a ten-year-old as an adolescent in transition to adulthood, so extending childhood to fifteen has no support in UN definitions.
evidence_level: Official definition of a UN agency

title: Convention on the Rights of the Child: Contact with Both Parents
source: United Nations, Convention on the Rights of the Child, 1989 (ratified by Egypt in 1990)

quotation.original: States Parties shall respect the right of the child who is separated from one or both parents to maintain personal relations and direct contact with both parents on a regular basis, except if it is contrary to the child's best interests.

why_it_matters: A binding treaty ratified by Egypt makes regular, direct contact with both parents a right of the child itself, not a privilege granted by one parent.

title: US National Library of Medicine: Puberty Begins at Eight in Girls and Nine in Boys
source: MedlinePlus — US National Library of Medicine, National Institutes of Health, 2026 (United States)

quotation.original: Puberty is the time in life when a boy or girl becomes sexually mature. It is a process that usually happens between ages 8 and 13 for girls and ages 9 and 14 for boys.

why_it_matters: The official US medical reference places normal puberty in girls between eight and thirteen, so nine — the Hanafi limit for a girl's custody by women — lies within the normal age of puberty.

title: US Study (2013): Onset of Puberty in Girls
source: Biro FM, et al., 2013, Pediatrics (United States)

quotation.original: Median age at onset of breast stage 2 was 8.8, 9.3, 9.7, and 9.7 years for African American, Hispanic, white non-Hispanic, and Asian participants, respectively. Girls with greater BMI reached breast stage 2 at younger ages.

why_it_matters: Median onset of puberty in girls falls between 8.8 and 9.7 years, a medical confirmation of nine as the limit of a girl's custody by women.

title: Copenhagen Puberty Study (2009): Puberty in Girls Now Begins Before Ten
source: Aksglaede L, Sørensen K, Petersen JH, Skakkebæk NE, Juul A, 2009, Pediatrics (Denmark)

quotation.original: Onset of puberty, defined as mean estimated age at attainment of glandular breast tissue (Tanner breast stage 2+), occurred significantly earlier in the 2006 cohort (estimated mean age: 9.86 years) when compared with the 1991 cohort (10.88 years).

why_it_matters: Within a single generation the onset of puberty in Danish girls fell by a full year to below ten, so nine is a real bodily threshold today.

title: American Dental Association: Shedding of Primary Incisors and Eruption of the First Permanent Molar at 6–7 Years
source: American Dental Association (ADA) — MouthHealthy, Eruption Charts, 2012 (United States)

quotation.original: Primary Tooth Development — Shed: Central incisor 6-7 yrs.; Lateral incisor 7-8 yrs. · Permanent Tooth Development — Erupt: First molar 6-7 yrs.; Central incisor 6-7 yrs. (lower), 7-8 yrs. (upper); Second molar 11-13 yrs. (lower), 12-13 yrs. (upper)

why_it_matters: The ADA dates the loss of the first milk teeth and the eruption of the first permanent molar to six to seven years — the dental change (ithghar) to which classical scholars tied discernment — and the second molar to the threshold of puberty.
evidence_level: Medical statement of a professional body

title: Lurie Children's Hospital (2023): Absent Paternal Acknowledgment on the Birth Certificate Raises Term Infant Mortality Across the United States
source: Prybylowski A, Howland J, Rankin KM, Collins JW Jr, 2023, Pediatrics — Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago and University of Illinois (United States)

quotation.original: The infant mortality rate of term births to US-born women with paternal nonacknowledgment equaled 5.0/1000 vs 2.0/1000 for those with paternal acknowledgment; relative risk (RR) = 2.47 (2.31, 2.86). ... Paternal nonacknowledgement is associated with a 40% greater infant mortality rate among term births to US-born and foreign-born women ... These findings highlight the importance of a father's involvement in the outcomes of infants born at term.

why_it_matters: National US birth records show term infant mortality about two and a half times higher when the father does not acknowledge the child, so the father matters from the first day of life.

title: Alio et al. (2011): Father Absence and Infant Mortality in the First Year
source: Alio AP, Mbah AK, Kornosky JL, Wathington D, Marty PJ, Salihu HM, 2011 — University of South Florida (United States)

quotation.original: infants born to black women with absent fathers had a seven-fold increased risk of infant mortality. Elevated risks of infant mortality were also observed for Hispanic infants with absent fathers (OR = 3.33, 95%CI = 2.66-4.17). About 65-75% of excess mortality could be prevented with increased paternal involvement. Paternal absence widens the black-white gap in infant mortality almost four-fold.

why_it_matters: Florida birth records show that father absence multiplies infant mortality, and that most of the excess deaths could be prevented through greater paternal involvement.

title: Academic Pediatrics (2018): Fathers Improve Children's Cognition and Mental Health and Reduce Obesity
source: Allport BS, Johnson S, Aqil A, Labrique AB, Nelson T, Kc A, et al., 2018, Academic Pediatrics — Johns Hopkins University (United States)

quotation.original: Paternal involvement in children's lives is associated with a variety of child outcomes, including improved cognition, improved mental health, reduced obesity rates, and asthma exacerbation. Given this evidence, the American Academy of Pediatrics has promoted actions by pediatricians to engage fathers in pediatric care.

why_it_matters: A Johns Hopkins review links paternal involvement to better cognition and mental health and lower obesity, which is why the American Academy of Pediatrics urges pediatricians to engage fathers.

title: Gordon and Feldman (2010): Fathers' Bonding Hormone Equals Mothers'
source: Gordon I, Zagoory-Sharon O, Leckman JF, Feldman R, 2010, Biological Psychiatry — Bar-Ilan University and Yale Child Study Center

quotation.original: Overall, parental OT increased across the study period and there were no differences between maternal and paternal OT at each time point. ... paternal OT correlated with the degree of stimulatory parenting behaviors, including proprioceptive contact, tactile stimulation, and object presentation.

why_it_matters: Oxytocin, the bonding hormone, rose equally in fathers and mothers with no difference at any time point, so the father's bond with his child is biological, not incidental.

title: Piaget: Ages Seven to Eight Are a Decisive Turning Point in Mental Development
source: Piaget J, 1972 — University of Geneva (Switzerland)

quotation.original: The age of seven to eight years, on average, marks a decisive turning point in the development …

why_it_matters: Piaget marks seven to eight as a decisive turning point, the onset of organized logical thinking — the same discernment (tamyiz) to which jurists tied the end of women's custody.

title: Vygotsky: The Crisis at Age Seven
source: Vygotsky LS, 1934, Collected Works (Russia)

quotation.original: School age, like all other age levels, opens with a critical or turning-point period; this was described in the literature as the crisis at age seven before the other age levels were described. It was noted that in making the transition from preschool to school age, the child changes abruptly and becomes more difficult with respect to rearing than he was previously. This is a kind of transitional stage—he is no longer a preschooler and not yet a school child.

why_it_matters: Vygotsky described the transition to school age as "the crisis at age seven", so seven is a recognized threshold in psychology and not in jurisprudence alone.

title: Laurence Steinberg: Adolescence Begins with Puberty
source: Steinberg L, 2014 — Temple University (United States)

quotation.original: Conventionally, "adolescence" has meant the stage of development that begins with puberty and ends with the economic and social independence of the young person from his or her parents. As I will explain, by that definition, ten to twenty-five isn't far off the mark today. [...] In this book, I use the term "adolescence" to refer to the period from ten until twenty-five.

why_it_matters: A leading scholar of adolescence defines adolescence as beginning with puberty, around ten, so fifteen is not childhood in psychology.
evidence_level: Scholarly book by a leading authority

title: Lamb (1977): Infants Attach to Their Fathers as to Their Mothers
source: Lamb ME, 1977, Child Development (United States)

quotation.original: Infants showed no preference for either parent in the display of attachment behaviors, though both parents were consistently differentiated from a relatively unfamiliar investigator on these measures. This indicates that infants were clearly attached to both parents from the beginning of attachment relations.

why_it_matters: Infants showed no preference for either parent in attachment behaviour, so a young child is attached to the father as much as to the mother from the beginning.

title: Michael Rutter: Maternal Deprivation Reassessed
source: Rutter M, 1972 — King's College London (United Kingdom)

quotation.original: The most parsimonious explanation of the research findings suggests that a child needs to have the presence of a person to whom he is attached but it is irrelevant whether or not this person is his mother. [...] If it is bond formation which is important (rather than mother-child bond formation), it is in a child's interest to encourage attachment to several people, not just one, so that if one person is away another is present.

why_it_matters: The founder of modern child psychiatry concluded that a child needs attachment figures, not the mother alone, and benefits from attachment to several people.

title: Warshak (2003): Asking Children Their Preference Does Not Reveal Their Best Interests but Makes Them Parties to Their Parents' Dispute
source: Warshak RA, 2003, Family Relations — University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center (United States)

quotation.original: This article discusses why most procedures for soliciting children's preferences do not reliably elicit information on their best interests and do not give children a meaningful voice in decision making. Instead, these procedures provide children with forums in which to takes sides in their parents' disputes. ... decision makers can use the collective voice of children, as revealed in research on such topics as joint custody, overnight stays, and relocation to help understand what children might say about these issues with the hindsight of maturity and in the absence of parental pressure, loyalty conflicts, inhibitions, and limitations in perspective and articulation.

why_it_matters: Soliciting a child's preference does not reliably reveal the child's interests and draws the child into the parental conflict; this grounds the principle that there can be no choice after exclusion of a parent.

title: Pediatrics (2002): An Unrelated Adult Man in the Home Raises the Risk of Death from Maltreatment Eightfold
source: Stiffman MN, Schnitzer PG, Adam P, Kruse RL, Ewigman BG. Household composition and risk of fatal child maltreatment. Pediatrics 2002;109(4):615

quotation.english: Children residing in households with adults unrelated to them were 8 times more likely to die of maltreatment than children in households with 2 biological parents.

why_it_matters: The leading paediatrics journal shows that a child living with an unrelated man, such as a mother's new husband, faces eight times the risk of death from maltreatment. Keeping a child from the father and in a stepfather's home exposes the child to grave danger.
evidence_level: Peer-reviewed study in the journal of the American Academy of Pediatrics

title: Meta-Analysis (2002): Adjustment of Children in Joint Custody
source: Bauserman R, 2002, Journal of Family Psychology (United States)

quotation.original: Children in joint physical or legal custody were better adjusted than children in sole-custody settings, but no different from those in intact families. More positive adjustment of joint-custody children held for separate comparisons of general adjustment, family relationships, self-esteem, emotional and behavioral adjustment, and divorce-specific adjustment. Joint-custody parents reported less current and past conflict than sole-custody parents, but this did not explain the better adjustment of joint-custody children.

why_it_matters: A meta-analysis of 33 studies found children in joint custody better adjusted than those in sole custody and no different from children in intact families.
evidence_level: Meta-analysis: the highest level of evidence

title: Hjern (2021): Multi-Year Follow-Up of More than 31,000 Danish Children
source: Hjern A, Urhoj SK, Fransson E, Bergström M, 2021 — Danish National Birth Cohort (Denmark)

quotation.original: Of the children who had experienced parental separation, children in joint physical custody had the lowest adjusted odds ratio (OR)1.25 (95%-CI 1.09-1.44), for a high SDQ score relative to children living in a nuclear family, with adjusted ORs of 1.63 (1.42-1.86) and OR 1.72 (1.52-1.95) for sole physical custody arrangements with and without a new partner.

why_it_matters: Among 31,519 children followed from seven to eleven, those in equal shared parenting were closest to children of intact families in mental health.

title: Bergström (2013): National Survey of More than 164,000 Pupils Aged Twelve and Fifteen
source: Bergström M, Modin B, Fransson E, Rajmil L, Berlin M, Gustafsson PA, Hjern A, 2013 — Stockholm University and Karolinska Institutet (Sweden)

quotation.original: Children in joint physical custody experienced more positive outcomes, in terms of subjective wellbeing, family life and peer relations, than children living mostly or only with one parent. ... Children who spent equal time living with both parents after a separation reported better wellbeing than children in predominantly single parent care. This was particularly true for the 15-year-olds

why_it_matters: Children in joint physical custody fared better than those living mostly with one parent, and this was especially true at fifteen.

title: Fransson, Hjern and Bergström (2018): The Research Record on Equal Shared Parenting after Separation
source: Fransson E, Hjern A, Bergström M, 2018, Journal of Divorce & Remarriage — Stockholm University (Sweden)

quotation.original: Children in JPC report better well-being and mental health than children who live mostly or only with 1 parent. No Swedish studies have found children's health to be worse in JPC than in sole parental care from child age of 3 years and beyond.

why_it_matters: The world's largest body of data on shared residence found no Swedish study in which children's health was worse in joint custody than in sole care from age three onward.

title: Study (2018): The Causal Effect of Joint Custody
source: Braver SL, Votruba AM, 2018, Journal of Divorce & Remarriage (United States)

quotation.original: On the basis of this comprehensive review we conclude that JPC probably does cause benefits to children on average, and that social scientists can now provisionally recommend rebuttably presumptive JPC to policymakers.

why_it_matters: A comprehensive review concluded that joint physical custody itself produces the benefit and recommended making it a rebuttable legal presumption.

title: Nielsen (2017): Conflict Does Not Rule Out Equal Shared Parenting
source: Nielsen L, 2017, Psychology, Public Policy, and Law (American Psychological Association) — Wake Forest University (United States)

quotation.original: Recent research does not support the idea that conflict—including high legal conflict—should rule out joint physical custody as the arrangement that best serves children's interests. [...] Conflict and poor coparenting are not linked to worse outcomes for children in joint physical custody than in sole physical custody. The quality of the parent–child relationship is a better predictor than conflict of children's outcomes, with the exception of the most extreme forms of conflict to which some children are exposed.

why_it_matters: Recent research does not support excluding joint physical custody because of parental conflict; the quality of each parent–child relationship matters more.

title: Fabricius (2020): A Child's Security with the Father Rises with Every Increment of Time Up to Equal Time
source: Fabricius WV, 2020, The Oxford Handbook of Children and the Law (Oxford University Press) — Arizona State University (United States)

quotation.original: young adults' current emotional security with their fathers improved with each increment, from 0% to 50%, of parenting time that they had spent with their fathers during childhood. ... Note that there is no 'plateau' short of equal parenting time that might indicate a minimum amount of parenting necessary to ensure good father-child relationships.

why_it_matters: Data from 1,030 young adults show emotional security with fathers improving with each increment of parenting time up to 50%, with no sufficient minimum short of equal time.
evidence_level: Chapter in a peer-reviewed academic handbook

title: Northern Finland Birth Cohort (2001): Growing Up Without One Parent Raises Male Mortality and Suicide
source: Sauvola A, et al., 2001, European Journal of Public Health — University of Oulu, Northern Finland 1966 Birth Cohort and national death register (Finland)

quotation.original: … the Northern Finland 1966 birth cohort which is linked with the national death register. … the general mortality risk for males with a single-parent family background was significantly increased compared with males from a two-parent family background (odds ratio 1.8 and 95% confidence interval: 1.1-2.9). The risk of committing suicide was significantly increased among young adult males with a single-parent family background (OR 2.5 and 95% CI: 1.1-5.8). … more preventative mental health support for children and adolescents living in broken homes.

why_it_matters: Young men from single-parent backgrounds had 1.8 times the mortality and 2.5 times the suicide risk, so losing a parent's presence endangers life, not only well-being.

title: Comanor and Phillips (2002): The Father's Presence in the Home Is the Most Important Protection Against Delinquency; Income Matters Far Less
source: Comanor WS, Phillips L, 2002, Journal of Applied Economics — National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (United States)

quotation.original: Using data from the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth, we estimate the impact of family income and various dimensions of family structure on a youth's contact with the criminal justice system between the ages of 14 and 22. From this analysis, we conclude that the single most important factor affecting these measures of delinquency is the presence of his father in the home. All other factors, including family income, are much less important.

why_it_matters: The single most important factor in a youth's contact with the criminal justice system was the father's presence at home; income mattered far less, so financial support cannot replace the father.
evidence_level: Peer-reviewed study of a national longitudinal survey

title: Antecol and Bedard (2007): Every Additional Five Years with the Father Lowers Smoking, Drug Use and Convictions
source: Antecol H, Bedard K, 2007, Journal of Population Economics — National Longitudinal Survey of Youth and Young Adult Supplement (United States)

quotation.original: There is longstanding evidence that youths raised by single parents are more likely to perform poorly in school and partake in “deviant” behaviors such as smoking, sex, substance use, and crime. … Using the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth and its Young Adult Supplement, we find that an additional 5 years with the biological father decreases the probability of smoking, drinking, engaging in sexual activity, marijuana use, and conviction by approximately 5.3, 1.2, 3.4, 2.2 and 0.3 percentage points, respectively.

why_it_matters: Each additional five years with the biological father measurably reduces smoking, drinking, early sexual activity, marijuana use and conviction.
evidence_level: Peer-reviewed study of a national longitudinal survey

title: European Court of Human Rights (2009): Granting the Mother Sole Custody Without Judicial Review Is Discrimination
source: European Court of Human Rights — Zaunegger v. Germany, no. 22028/04, 2009 (Council of Europe)

quotation.original: the mutual enjoyment by a parent and child of each other's company constitutes a fundamental element of family life, even if the relationship between the parents has broken down ... there was not a reasonable relationship of proportionality between the general exclusion of judicial review of the initial attribution of sole custody to the mother and the aim pursued

why_it_matters: The Court held that automatically vesting sole custody in the mother, with no judicial review of the father's share, is discriminatory; Germany amended its Civil Code in 2013 as a result.
evidence_level: Binding judgment of an international court

title: German Federal Court of Justice (2017): Equal Alternating Residence May Be Ordered Despite One Parent's Objection
source: Bundesgerichtshof (Federal Court of Justice), Beschluss XII ZB 601/15, 2017 (Germany)

quotation.original: Das Wechselmodell ist anzuordnen, wenn die geteilte Betreuung durch beide Eltern im Vergleich mit anderen Betreuungsmodellen dem Kindeswohl im konkreten Fall am besten entspricht. ... Eine zum paritätischen Wechselmodell führende Umgangsregelung steht vielmehr mit dem gemeinsamen Sorgerecht im Einklang, zumal beide Eltern gleichberechtigte Inhaber der elterlichen Sorge sind
quotation.english: The alternating residence model is to be ordered if shared care by both parents, compared with other care models, best serves the child's welfare in the specific case. … A contact arrangement leading to an equal alternating residence model is, rather, consistent with joint parental custody, especially since both parents hold parental custody with equal rights.

why_it_matters: Germany's highest civil court held that equal alternating residence can be ordered over one parent's objection when it best serves the child, because both parents hold parental authority equally.

title: Spanish Supreme Court (2013): Joint Custody Is the Norm
source: Tribunal Supremo (Supreme Court), Civil Chamber, Judgment 257/2013, 2013 (Spain)

quotation.original: La redacción del artículo 92 no permite concluir que [la guarda y custodia compartida] se trate de una medida excepcional, sino que al contrario, habrá de considerarse normal e incluso deseable, porque permite que sea efectivo el derecho que los hijos tienen a relacionarse con ambos progenitores, aun en situaciones de crisis, siempre que ello sea posible y en tanto en cuanto lo sea.
quotation.english: The wording of Article 92 does not allow the conclusion that [shared custody] is an exceptional measure; on the contrary, it must be considered normal and even desirable, because it makes effective the right that children have to maintain relations with both parents, even in situations of crisis, whenever this is possible and to the extent that it is.

why_it_matters: Spain's Supreme Court held that joint custody is the normal and desirable arrangement because it gives effect to children's right to relations with both parents.

title: European Court of Human Rights, Grand Chamber (2000): A Five-Year-Old's Rejection of His Father Cannot Be Decisive Without Psychological Expertise
source: European Court of Human Rights, Grand Chamber — Elsholz v. Germany, no. 25735/94, 2000 (Council of Europe)

quotation.original: the mutual enjoyment by parent and child of each other's company constitutes a fundamental element of family life, even if the relationship between the parents has broken down ... taking into account the importance of the subject matter, namely, the relations between a father and his child, the Regional Court should not have been satisfied, in the circumstances, with relying on the file and the written appeal submissions without having at its disposal psychological expert evidence in order to evaluate the child's statements.

why_it_matters: Denying a father contact on the strength of a young child's stated refusal, without psychological expert evidence, violated the father's rights; a child's stated wish is not decisive on its own.
evidence_level: Binding judgment of an international court

title: Andhra Pradesh High Court (1982): Under Islamic Law, the Father Is Entitled to Custody of a Boy After Seven
source: High Court of Andhra Pradesh, Division Bench (Letters Patent Appeal), judgment by Raghuvir J., 1982 (India)

quotation.original: Under Muslim law, after the age of 7 years, it is the father who is entitled to the custody of the child, unless the Court holds on evidence, the father is not a fit person or that it is not conducive to the health whether physical or mental of the child. … Ordinarily, the children are to be with the father. … The child is above seven years. … We are of the view that on the evidence since nothing is brought out against the father to show he is unfit we hold, he is entitled to the custody of the child.

why_it_matters: A court applying Islamic law held that after seven the father is entitled to custody and that "ordinarily, the children are to be with the father", and ordered the boy handed to him.

title: Telangana High Court (2024): The Father Is Entitled to Custody After Seven and Is the Natural Guardian
source: High Court for the State of Telangana, Division Bench — P. Sam Koshy and Sambasivarao Naidu JJ., 2024 (India)

quotation.original: Under Muslim law, after the age of 7 years, it is the father who is entitled to the custody of the child, unless the Court holds on evidence, the father is not a fit person or that is not conducive to the health whether physical or mental of the child. Ordinarily, the children are to be with the father. … the mother is having absolute custody with regard to female child until she attains puberty … Being the natural biological father undisputedly the respondent is the natural guardian also.

why_it_matters: A 2024 judgment restates the rule that after seven the father is entitled to custody and is the natural guardian, while widening the maternal grandparents' visitation.

title: Bombay High Court (2007): Custody of a Boy Over Seven Goes to the Father; the Minor's Wish Is Not Decisive
source: High Court of Judicature at Bombay — V.R. Kingaonkar J., 2007 (India)

quotation.original: all the three minor sons are willing to continue their association with the mother and want to live with her … it does not mean that mere willingness of the minor would be dicisive factor. … The custody of male child over seven years of age will have to be given to the father … The appellant has proved that he is a fit person. … Child -Sayyad Danish be given in custody of the appellant -Sayyad Sabdarali, if he would furnish an undertaking … the child will be admitted in a standard school at Bhusawal or nereby area

why_it_matters: The Court gave the son over seven to his father, on condition of enrolment in a regular school and with the mother's weekly visits, while the younger children stayed with their mother — an age-based division matching classical jurisprudence.

title: Al-Durr al-Mukhtar: Seven and Nine — "And on This the Fatwa Is Given"
source: Al-Haskafi (d. 1088 AH), Al-Durr al-Mukhtar — Hanafi school

quotation.english: (The female custodian), whether the mother or another, (has the better right to him), that is, to the boy, until he no longer needs women; this was estimated at seven, and on this the fatwa is given, because it is the usual case. If they disagree about his age, then if he eats, drinks, dresses and cleans himself alone, he is handed over to him [the father], even by compulsion; otherwise not. … (And the others have the better right to her until she becomes desirable), and this was estimated at nine, and on this the fatwa is given. (And from Muhammad [al-Shaybani]: the ruling for the mother and the grandmother is the same), and on this the fatwa is given because of widespread corruption — [as stated by] al-Zayla'i.

why_it_matters: This is the position on which fatwas are given in the Hanafi school applied in Egypt: seven for the boy and nine for the girl.

title: Al-Bahr al-Ra'iq: The Fatwa Is on Seven Because the Father Is Commanded to Order Him to Pray
source: Ibn Nujaym, Al-Bahr al-Ra'iq — Hanafi school

quotation.english: In Ghayat al-Bayan, al-Tabyin and al-Kafi it is stated that the fatwa follows the view of al-Khassaf, namely the estimation at seven, because the father is commanded to order him to pray when he reaches it, and that can only happen if the child is with him.

why_it_matters: Ibn Nujaym grounds the age of seven in the Prophetic command to teach prayer at seven, which the father can only fulfil if the child lives with him.

title: Kashshaf al-Qina': Seven Was Chosen Because It Is the First Stage at Which the Law Addresses the Child with Prayer
source: Mansur ibn Yunus al-Buhuti (d. 1051 AH), Kashshaf al-Qina' — Hanbali school (relied upon for fatwa)

quotation.english: (Section: When the boy reaches seven years of sound mind and his parents agree that he stay with one of them, that is permitted), because the right to his custody belongs to them both and does not go beyond them. (If they dispute) — that is, the parents — (over him) — that is, over his custody — (the judge gives him the choice between them, and he stays with whichever of them he chooses) … It was tied to seven because it is the first stage at which the Law commands that he be addressed with prayer, unlike the mother, who was given precedence in early childhood because of his need to be carried and directly served, since she knows that best.

why_it_matters: The text ties the custody limit expressly to the age of the command to pray and explains the mother's precedence by the young child's physical needs; when those needs end, so does the precedence.
evidence_level: Authoritative juristic text (principal fatwa reference of the Hanbali school)

title: Fatwa of the Grand Mufti Ahmad Hureidi (1967): Women's Right of Custody Is Limited to Seven for the Boy and Nine for the Girl
source: Egyptian Dar al-Ifta — Grand Mufti Ahmad Hureidi, 1967; official collection of the Fatwas of Dar al-Ifta (Egypt)

quotation.english: The right of custody belongs to women from the birth of the young child until a specified age, set at seven years for the boy and nine years for the girl. … 4 – If she refuses to hand him over, she is ordered by the judge to do so if the matter is brought before him.

why_it_matters: Egypt's official fatwa authority still affirmed in 1967 that women's custody is limited to seven and nine, and that a custodian who refuses to hand over the child is ordered to do so by the judge.
evidence_level: Official fatwa of the State Mufti

title: Al-Abyani: The Child Is Handed to the Father at Seven and Nine, and the Father Is Compelled to Take Him
source: Muhammad Zayd al-Abyani (d. 1355 AH), commentary on Qadri Pasha's codification of personal status rules — Hanafi school (Egypt)

quotation.english: The Lawgiver has ruled that the child stays with the custodian until he no longer needs the service of women, and this was estimated at his reaching seven years. If male, his custody period has ended; if female, she remains with her two more years to be trained in the household matters that will be required of her in the future. Then each of them is handed to the father, and if he does not ask for them he is compelled to take them, because the young child's right attaches to him; for the male, after reaching the age of discernment, needs to learn what benefits him, and the female, after reaching the age of desirability, needs protection, and there is no doubt that the father is more capable of that …

why_it_matters: The commentator whose work underpinned Egypt's former Sharia courts makes the transfer to the father at seven and nine a right of the child, enforceable against the father himself.

title: Al-Mudawwana: The Father Educates Him by Day and He Sleeps at His Mother's
source: Imam Malik, as transmitted by Ibn al-Qasim in Al-Mudawwana — Maliki school

quotation.english: He said: Malik said: He [the father] educates him by day and sends him to the Qur'an school, and he returns to his mother at night in her custody; he educates him while he is with his mother and looks after him while he is with his mother, and he is not separated from her unless she remarries.

why_it_matters: Imam Malik himself describes a divided arrangement — days with the father for education, nights with the mother — showing that the Maliki school does not keep the father away from his child until puberty.

title: Al-Kafi: At Seven the Girl Stays with Her Father Without Being Given a Choice
source: Ibn Qudama, Al-Kafi — Hanbali school

quotation.english: "When the girl reaches seven, she is left with the father without being given a choice, because her interest lies in being with her father: she needs protection, and the father is more fit for it, and she is approaching suitability for marriage, and she is sought in marriage from her father, since he is her guardian and holds the power to give her in marriage." "She stays with him night and day, because her upbringing and training take place in the home, and the mother is not prevented from visiting her." "If she falls ill, the mother has the better right to nurse her in her own home … and if the mother falls ill, the girl is not prevented from visiting her." "And if she is a girl, her father may prevent her from living alone, because it cannot be guaranteed that corrupt people will not reach her."

why_it_matters: Ibn Qudama places the girl with her father at seven without a choice because her interest lies in his protection, while preserving the mother's visits and her right to nurse the girl.

title: Islamic Family Law of Malaysia (1984): Women's Custody Ends at Seven for a Boy and Nine for a Girl
source: Islamic Family Law (Federal Territories) Act 1984 (Malaysia)

quotation.original: (1) The right of the hadhinah to the custody of a child terminates upon the child attaining the age of seven years, in the case of a male, and the age of nine years, in the case of a female … (2) After termination of the right of the hadhinah, the custody devolves upon the father, and if the child has reached the age of discernment (mumaiyiz), he or she shall have the choice of living with either of the parents, unless the Court otherwise orders.

why_it_matters: A contemporary Muslim-majority state codifies the classical rule in force today: custody by the female custodian ends at seven for a boy and nine for a girl, and then passes to the father.

title: Abu Dhabi: Joint Custody as the Default
source: Abu Dhabi Civil Personal Status Law, 2021, applied by the Abu Dhabi Family Court (United Arab Emirates)

quotation.english: Custody of the children is a joint and equal right of the father and the mother after divorce occurs. / The default in custody of the children is the joint participation of the father and the mother in the responsibility of raising the children after divorce occurs, unless one of them requests in writing before the court to waive his or her right of custody, or applies to the court to remove the other party from joint custody and terminate his or her right of custody.

why_it_matters: Abu Dhabi makes joint and equal custody the default after divorce, showing that equal shared parenting is already law in an Arab jurisdiction.

title: Official Spanish Statistics (2025 data): Joint Custody in More than Half of Divorces — 50.8%
source: Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE), Statistics on Annulments, Separations and Divorces, published 2026 (Spain)

quotation.original: La custodia compartida fue otorgada en el 50,8% de los casos de divorcio de parejas con hijos, 1,1 puntos más que en el año anterior. … En el 3,4% de estos divorcios la custodia se otorgó al padre, en el 45,3% a la madre, en el 50,8% fue compartida y en el 0,5% se otorgó a otras instituciones o familiares. Cabe destacar que los casos de custodia compartida siguen su tendencia creciente, superando a aquellos en los que la custodia se otorgó a la madre.
quotation.english: Joint custody was granted in 50.8% of divorce cases of couples with children, 1.1 points more than the previous year. … In 3.4% of these divorces custody was granted to the father, in 45.3% to the mother, in 50.8% it was shared, and in 0.5% it was granted to other institutions or relatives. It is worth noting that joint custody cases continue their upward trend, exceeding those in which custody was granted to the mother.

why_it_matters: In Spain, alternating-residence joint custody is now the most common outcome of divorces involving children, ahead of sole maternal custody.

title: Arkansas Law (2021): Presumption of Joint Custody
source: Arkansas Act 604 of 2021, amending Ark. Code § 9-13-101 (United States)

quotation.original: (iv)(a) In an action concerning an original child custody determination in a divorce or paternity matter, there is a rebuttable presumption that joint custody is in the best interest of the child. (b) The presumption that joint custody is in the best interest of the child may be rebutted: (1) If the court finds by clear and convincing evidence that joint custody is not in the best interest of the child; — and § 9-13-101(a)(5): "joint custody" means the approximate and reasonable equal division of time with the child by both parents individually as agreed to by the parents or as ordered by the court.

why_it_matters: Arkansas makes joint custody — an approximately equal division of time — a presumption rebuttable only by clear and convincing evidence.

title: Council of Europe (2015): Shared Residence as the Default
source: Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe, Resolution, 2015

quotation.original: [The Assembly calls on the member States to] introduce into their laws the principle of shared residence following a separation, limiting any exceptions…

why_it_matters: Parliamentarians from 46 European states call on member states to introduce the principle of shared residence after separation into law, with limited exceptions.
